We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We have applied 29646 to target, got three possible precursors (three outcomes). We need to choose one that can be further processed with next template 1914389, then 1914390, then 149040, then 1914391.

We applied 1914389 to one of the outcomes (the one with silyl protecting group). It gave two products: a precursor and a side product? The result tuple: (('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C', 'CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC'),). So applying 1914389 to the silyl-protected intermediate gave two fragments: the main fragment (still silyl protected) and a side fragment (an ester with phosphonate). That seems odd; maybe the template is a disconnection that splits the molecule into two pieces.

Now we need to apply 1914390 to something. We tried applying to the main fragment but got no result. Maybe we need to apply 1914390 to the side fragment? Let's try applying 1914390 to 'CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC'. It gave no result earlier. So maybe we need to choose a different outcome from 29646.

Let's examine the three outcomes from 29646:

Result: (('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO',))

Actually the three strings are similar but differ in placement of silyl group. The first two are same? Might be duplicates.

We need a route of 5 steps. Perhaps we can design a synthetic plan: target -> (29646) gives a protected intermediate (with silyl). Then (1914389) splits off a side chain (phosphonate). Then (1914390) maybe does something to that side chain? But we got no result.

Maybe we need to apply 1914390 to the main fragment after deprotecting? Or maybe we need to apply 149040 next to the main fragment, then 1914391.

Let's try applying 149040 to the main fragment (the silyl-protected). Already did: got two fragments: main fragment (still silyl) and a sulfonyl fluoride? Actually result: ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO', 'CC(C)(C)[Si](C)(C)OS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F') So it splits off a silyl sulfonyl fluoride group.

Now we need to apply 1914391 to something. Let's see what 1914391 does. We need to apply to one of the fragments maybe.

Let's try applying 1914391 to the fragment 'C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO'.
